subject: physics

sections.title: Introduction to Circuits and DC Instruments
learning_objectives: Draw a circuit with resistors in parallel and in series.

sections.title: Resistors in Series and Parallel
learning_objectives: Draw a circuit with resistors in parallel and in series.
Calculate the voltage drop of a current across a resistor using Ohm’s law.
Contrast the way total resistance is calculated for resistors in series and in parallel.
Explain why total resistance of a parallel circuit is less than the smallest resistance of any of the resistors in that circuit.
Calculate total resistance of a circuit that contains a mixture of resistors connected in series and in parallel.

sections.title: Electromotive Force: Terminal Voltage
learning_objectives: Compare and contrast the voltage and the electromagnetic force of an electric power source.
Describe what happens to the terminal voltage, current, and power delivered to a load as internal resistance of the voltage source increases (due to aging of batteries, for example).
Explain why it is beneficial to use more than one voltage source connected in parallel.

sections.title: Kirchhoff’s Rules
learning_objectives: Analyze a complex circuit using Kirchhoff’s rules, using the conventions for determining the correct signs of various terms.

sections.title: DC Voltmeters and Ammeters
learning_objectives: Explain why a voltmeter must be connected in parallel with the circuit.
Draw a diagram showing an ammeter correctly connected in a circuit.
Describe how a galvanometer can be used as either a voltmeter or an ammeter.
Find the resistance that must be placed in series with a galvanometer to allow it to be used as a voltmeter with a given reading.
Explain why measuring the voltage or current in a circuit can never be exact.

sections.title: Null Measurements
learning_objectives: Explain why a null measurement device is more accurate than a standard voltmeter or ammeter.
Demonstrate how a Wheatstone bridge can be used to accurately calculate the resistance in a circuit.

sections.title: DC Circuits Containing Resistors and Capacitors
learning_objectives: Explain the importance of the time constant, τ , and calculate the time constant for a given resistance and capacitance.
Explain why batteries in a flashlight gradually lose power and the light dims over time.
Describe what happens to a graph of the voltage across a capacitor over time as it charges.
Explain how a timing circuit works and list some applications.
Calculate the necessary speed of a strobe flash needed to “stop” the movement of an object over a particular length.

misconception.text: Current is used up as it goes round a circuit.

correction.text: The same current flows at every point of a series circuit. What is used up is the energy, not the current.

signal.text: Our own teaching of the section, waiting for a paper question that shows the same mistake.

misconception.text: Putting a resistor in a series circuit changes the current everywhere.

correction.text: It does, and that is why a series resistor dims the whole circuit rather than one lamp.
